messages:
devin: quick brain-dump: we keep drifting between two patterns for hosted/dedicated/private gating: 1) runtime-declared capabilities (what i called 'capability-first') and 2) policy-first routing (control-plane decides what to route based on tenant policy). want to pick one canonical flow for the next quarter.

helen: can you clarify differences operationally? e.g., what does operator do for private installs?

devin: capability-first = runtime advertises what it can do (quant level, kv-cache, accel), control-plane picks compatible model variant. policy-first = control-plane says "only route low-latency to these nodes" and runtime just enforces. capability-first reduces churn when infra changes, policy-first gives more control for compliance.

oscar: security angle: capability-first requires we trust runtime metadata. how do we prevent an operator in a private deploy from lying about capabilities to get routed high-cost traffic?

sec-bot: security note: any runtime-declared capability must be signed and attestable. recommend TPM/KMS attestation or signed manifest uploaded during onboarding.

helen: reality for private on-prem customers: they prefer a simple install path. asking them to wire up attestation isn't realistic at first. maybe a hybrid: manifest on install + optional periodic signed probe.

devin: hybrid sounds pragmatic. manifest (static) = offline onboarding source of truth. probe (dynamic) = runtime pings control-plane for ephemeral capability updates.

oscar: tradeoffs: manifest stale vs probe network requirements. Also need to define TTL and precedence rules (which wins when manifest and probe disagree).

helen: proposal: precedence = probe (fresh) > manifest (install-time) > control-plane fallback policy. require signed probe responses when customer opts-in for attestation; otherwise mark as "unattested" and subject to stricter routing (e.g., no burst to quantized variants).

devin: good. need to design the routing decision matrix. minimal example table in text:
```
routing decision inputs: [tenant_policy, capability_set, attestation_state]
if attestation_state == unattested -> only route to baseline models
else consult tenant_policy + capability_set for allowed variants
```

oscar: metrics/observability: we should emit a capability-fingerprint histogram per runtime + tenant-hash (no PII). surface mismatches as alerts.

helen: what about dedicated (reserved capacity) customers? they expect absolute predictability and dedicated pools. routing there should be unaffected by runtime claims: control-plane must honor reservation and only use capabilities for optional optimizations (e.g., use kv-cache feature if available).

devin: agreed. add a note: dedicated pools have hard constraints: routing must prioritize commit units first. capability gates only for performance tuning, not admission.

oscar: compatibility with sidecar vs no-sidecar: sidecar option gives us local cached manifests + enforced policy at the node. no-sidecar requires stronger networked control-plane checks. need to list features that require sidecar (local prompt caching, offline retry) vs features that are fine without it (streaming, basic generation).

helen: let's create a features matrix. early draft items:
- local-prefix-cache -> sidecar required
- fast fallbacks (0-1s) -> sidecar recommended
- telemetry enrichment -> sidecar optional
- capability probe -> runtime endpoint or sidecar proxy

devin: security/crypto specifics: signed-manifest format (detached JWS), probe responses signed with short-lived key; recommend key rotation every 7 days for lease keys; longer (90d) for install manifests.

oscar: also surface what happens on disagreement: control-plane must log incident and reduce routing privileges, then create a human ticket for ops. auto-remediation only if signature verification fails consistently for > 3 tries.

ops: practical ops checklist for private customers: (1) upload signed manifest on install, (2) expose probe endpoint optionally on management network, (3) provide TLS certs or mTLS for probe when possible, (4) document how to opt into attestations.

helen: small sample manifest snippet (install-time):
```json
{
  "tenant": "tenant-hash:abc123",
  "capabilities": ["streaming", "kv-cache:1"],
  "issued_by": "redwood-enterprise-installer",
  "issued_at": "2026-02-03T12:00:00Z",
  "signature": "<detached-jws>"
}
```

devin: follow-ups: I'll draft a one-pager + a routing-decision-state-machine diagram. we need to be explicit about what "unattested" means and precise metric names.

oscar: ping security to review manifest JWS policy: @sec-bot please flag required claims.

sec-bot: flagged. will push a checklist: required claims = issuer, tenant-hash, capabilities, expiry, signing-key-id. also require a revocation URL if customer rotates keys.

helen: timeline: draft by Mon, review Wed, aim to include in the hosted/dedicated/private RFC bundle by next sprint.

devin: thanks all. created ticket: https://tickets.internal/redwood/INF-1428 to track the matrix + sample code.

oscar: :thumbsup:
